long_biography.plain_text:
Scanomat began as Preben Vibe-Petersen's Danish family enterprise in 1961. Kim joined that established platform and became the engineer behind its defining technological shift. In 1981, he designed a fully automatic cappuccino system, moving the business beyond imported and serviced vending equipment toward proprietary beverage machinery.

He subsequently led development of TopBrewer, an under-counter platform combining mechanical dispensing with software control. Patent records name him personally as inventor, while the intellectual property belongs to Scanomat. Vibe-Petersen now serves as chief executive and ultimate capital owner, with a later generation also involved in management. His wider structure includes investment, real-estate and maritime companies, but their balance sheets and operating property remain corporate assets. The same boundary applies to factories, coffee-roasting operations, patents, leased property and any hospitality ventures. These interests show diversification rather than a replacement for Scanomat: automated beverage manufacturing remains the business most closely tied to his ownership, daily leadership and wealth creation.

Kim is personally named as inventor or designer on beverage-system records, but Scanomat is the applicant or assignee. The patents and registrations are therefore treated as company intellectual property rather than his standalone personal assets.

Annual reports identify Kim as ultimate capital owner of the Scanomat chain and disclose commercial property that he personally leases to the group. Corporate factories, cash, debt, revenue, group investments and subsidiary assets remain distinct from his personal property.
